what: A text repair of mine destroyed a section heading of the report, and 21 of the 22 checkers then in service reported the build clean. The regression is documented here together with the three checker weaknesses that allowed it.
how_it_happened: The report is generated by concatenating _bodyN.py parts, and the repair of a tautology in section 1 was done by addressing lines by number. Two lines were overwritten before the duplicate was spotted, and one of them was the H1("2. Инструментальная среда и замечание о замене САПР") statement. Removing it took the paragraph count from 231 to 230.
how_detected: Not by any checker. The battery output showed "paragraphs: 230" where every previous build had shown 231, and I refused to treat that as noise: a count that moves by exactly one during a text-only edit needs an explanation. lab13/_para_diff.py then aligned the current document against the delivered copy with difflib and reported the deleted heading by name.

checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.flaw: the section binding test was `h.startswith(sec) or sec in h`. For a single-digit section such as "2", the substring test matches every heading containing the digit 2 - "3.2", "5.2", "8.2" - so the check was vacuous and reported all 41 requirements covered with the owning heading absent.
checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.fix: binding made exact: the heading number is parsed off first and the remainder must begin with the label, so a label can only match at the start of a heading. Both shapes are supported, by number ("5.3") and by label ("Задание 1" in "5. Задание 1: ..."), because the report uses both.
checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.self_test: 6 planted cases, 6 correct: three legitimate bindings accepted, three illegitimate rejected (a label in a different task heading, a bare digit in an unrelated sub-section, a wrong sub-section of the same top-level section).

checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.flaw: it printed "unmet: 5" and still exited 0. A checker that reports a problem and returns success cannot participate in a battery whose pass criterion is the exit code.
checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.fix: raises SystemExit on any unmet requirement.

checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.flaw: every checker tested content that is PRESENT. None asked whether every section of the plan exists, so a deletion was invisible by construction.
checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.fix: lab13/_struct.py added: it asserts the heading tree against the 37-section plan (none missing, none unexpected, none duplicated, numbering monotonic, and every Heading-N paragraph carrying an N-level number). Its self-test simulates deleting sections 2, 5.4 and 9.2 and requires all three to be reported missing.
checker_weaknesses_that_allowed_it.note: the level check in the first draft of _struct.py zipped a list of numeric headings against a list of all headings, so it compared the wrong pairs; it was rewritten to walk the paragraphs directly. Recorded because a check written carelessly is worse than no check.

text_defects_found_in_the_same_pass.kind: ё omitted where the report writes ё systematically (104 distinct words, 273 tokens)

_audit2.py: repeated-word threshold lowered from 3 to 2 characters, and table cells now scanned too - the old threshold excluded exactly the short function words where this typo is commonest, which is why "во во всех" survived every earlier run
missing space after a sentence terminator, guarded so that net names (N0.OUT, NR.IN) are not mistaken for stops
missing space after a comma, case-insensitive - the first version looked only for capitals and therefore could not catch its own planted "…цифрах,а на…"
a word repeated across a number in the same clause, which is the tautology shape the generator produces
self-test: 6 planted defects, all caught; 10 correct sentences, no false positives
_yo2.py: criterion replaced: the first version tested only pure inconsistency (a word occurring both with ё and with е) and reported 0 on a document containing two real defects, because those words occur only in their е-form. The new criterion measures the document's own convention first and then flags a stem that must carry ё without it.
short participles excluded: "разряжены", "заряжены", "разрешены" take no ё because the stress falls on the ending; only the full form does
the scan and the self-test now call the SAME classify() function - the second version tested a helper the scan did not use, so the test proved nothing

honest_limits: the ё lexicon is declared and deliberately not exhaustive: it covers only the word families this report uses, so a defect in an uncovered family would still pass
the oblique-case exemption in the numeral-agreement checker remains approximate, since a regular expression cannot decline Russian

the paragraph-count anomaly that exposed the deleted heading was found by a human noticing a number move by one, not by any check; _struct.py closes that specific hole, but the general lesson is that a battery with no negative-existence test trusts every count it is not asked about

state_after_repair.battery: 24 / 24 checkers EXIT=0, every one of them carrying a mandatory self-test that plants known-bad input
state_after_repair.paragraph_diff_against_delivered_copy: one intentional replacement (the section 4.3 wording), no deletions

build_reference.note: Any other sha256 in this file is a measurement of an earlier build and is labelled as historical where it appears; it has deliberately not been rewritten, because rewriting a recorded measurement would falsify it.
